metadata.agent_last_message:
The implementation is complete. Here's a summary of what was built:

**Project structure** at `output/`:
- `Cargo.toml` (no dependencies)
- `src/main.rs` — CLI orchestration (371 lines)
- `src/cli.rs` — argument parsing (122 lines)
- `src/bib.rs` — `.bib` database parser with crossref resolution (596 lines)
- `src/bst.rs` — `.bst` lexer/parser with symbol table (667 lines)
- `src/interp.rs` — stack-based interpreter implementing all 37 built-ins (972 lines)
- `src/name.rs` — name parsing, `format.name$`, `purify$`, `width$`, `text.length$`, `text.prefix$` (1025 lines)
- `src/output.rs` — output buffer with 79-column line wrapping (112 lines)
- `src/json.rs` — JSON encoder (78 lines)
- `src/widths.rs` — cmr10 character widths from `bibtex.web §13` (115 lines)
- `src/diag.rs` — Warning/Error types (84 lines)

**Verified behaviors**:
- All four canonical styles (plain, alpha, unsrt, abbrv) produce sensible output
- Author name parsing for all 3 forms (no comma, 1 comma, 2 commas), including von names like "de la Vallée Poussin" and special chars like "{\AA}kerman"
- Crossref inheritance with unresolved-crossref warnings
- @string macro expansion, including .bst-defined MACROs in scope when parsing .bib
- @preamble accumulation
- 79-column line wrapping with backward + forward fallback
- alpha.bst label generation (e.g. `[ABC{\etalchar{+}}20]` for 5+ authors)
- "and others" → et~al. detection
- Title case-conversion respecting brace protection
- JSON log with all required fields and warning kinds matching the spec's canonical strings
- Exit codes 0/1/2 per spec
- `--cites` (with `#` comments and blank lines) and `--aux` (parsing `\citation{}` commands), with concatenation and dedup

Build cleanly with no warnings via `cargo build --release --manifest-path output/Cargo.toml`.

    def run_bibtex(

        timeout: int = 30,

            args += ["--cites", str(cites_file)]

            args += ["--log", str(log_file)]
